clue.text: Settle your debts now that there has been a wage rise

definitions.meaning: an urgent demand to hand over money owed

definitions.text: there has been a wage rise
definitions.meaning: salaries have gone higher, read as a phrase describing earnings

explanation.surface: A creditor insists on payment now that the debtor has had a raise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an imperative to clear what is owed and a description of earnings increasing.

clue.text: A theologian showed the way to describe his curate's egg

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
to lead is to show the way; past tense led

explanation.surface: A clergyman leads the way to talk about his curate's breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'curate's egg' is the proverbial egg that is good in parts, i.e. partly rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten egg is called addled, the word one would use to describe the bad egg the curate was served.

clue.text: One who sticks by woman in a depression

indicators.note: the word woman sits inside the depression, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dent is a small depression in a surface
her is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter stays with a woman who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood, but it is a physical dent.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or follower is someone who sticks loyally to a cause or person.

clue.text: Which man in the cricket team finds time for grousing?

definitions.text: Which man in the cricket team
definitions.meaning: the reserve player in cricket, who fields as a substitute beyond the eleven
the Glorious ..., 12 August, opens the British grouse-shooting season

explanation.surface: A cricket question about which player finds time to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grousing' looks like grumbling, but it means shooting grouse; the season opens on 12 August, the Glorious Twelfth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's reserve is the extra man after eleven, and the grouse season's opening date is the twelfth of August.

clue.text: Radical church painter

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter who belongs to a radical church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a 19th-century British movement demanding political reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartists campaigned for votes for all men and other reforms, so one is a radical.

clue.text: Heavy metal found on Gibraltar

parts.note: heavy metal is a genre of loud guitar music, and Gibraltar is known as the Rock, so its music is jokingly that of the Rock

explanation.surface: A mineral deposit discovered on Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' looks like lead or similar, but it is the music genre; Gibraltar is nicknamed the Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy metal is a loud style of guitar-led popular music, and Gibraltar's nickname supplies the other half.

clue.text: How totally successful men win apparently without raising a finger

definitions.meaning: an easy, overwhelming victory is won this way
with the palms lowered, literally idle

explanation.surface: Champions seem to triumph without any effort at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means easily and decisively, and literally pictures palms kept low and unused.

clue.text: Western director's order to actors and cameramen

definitions.text: Western director's order to actors and cameramen

parts.words: Western director's order to actors and cameramen
parts.note: the command to start filming a scene, which in a cowboy film is also the gunfight call

explanation.surface: A film director on a cowboy picture calls out to the cast and crew.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Western the word also means fire your guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Directors tell the crew to film, and in a Western the same word means fire guns.

clue.text: Employer who disheartens the usher

indicators.note: to dishearten is read as removing the heart, the central letter of the word usher

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boss who discourages the doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartens' looks like discourages, but it means take out the middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever employs a tool or service makes use of it.

clue.text: Without doubt it means the village can withstand drought

definitions.meaning: very definitely, as in knowing something perfectly

definitions.text: it means the village can withstand drought
definitions.meaning: a brimming water source keeps a village supplied in dry weather

explanation.surface: A village is certainly safe from a dry spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means certainly, and a brimming water source lets a village survive dry weather.

clue.text: An oarsman to be feared by those of faint heart

definitions.meaning: the rower nearest the stern who sets the pace

definitions.text: to be feared by those of faint heart
definitions.meaning: a sudden seizure such as apoplexy threatens people with weak hearts

explanation.surface: A rower who frightens timid people.
explanation.definitionFit: The pace-setting rower has this title, and the same word names a sudden medical seizure feared by those with weak hearts.

clue.text: Was bone lazy and lied indiscriminately

indicators.note: without order or selection, so the letters of lied are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was very lazy and told careless lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing no work at all, inactive and slothful.

clue.text: Desist from advising on how to check a word in the dictionary

definitions.meaning: stop it, a slang command to cease

definitions.text: advising on how to check a word in the dictionary
definitions.meaning: telling someone to look the word up in the book

explanation.surface: Stop telling people how to use a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means stop it, and literally tells someone to find a word by searching the pages.

clue.text: Drunken barrister resistant to water

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a waterproof fabric; the definition describes it

parts.note: oiled is slang for drunk
a silk is a Queen's Counsel, a senior barrister who wears a silk gown

explanation.surface: A drunk lawyer is impervious to water.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior barrister (QC or KC) is called a silk after the gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric treated with oil to make it waterproof was used for raincoats and dressings.

clue.text: Very religious fellows need to develop a certain spice

parts.note: PI is short for pious, very religious
men are fellows
taken as written

explanation.surface: Devout men must grow a particular spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice, the dried berry of a Caribbean tree, is also known by this name.

clue.text: The hangman who has a will to discharge

definitions.meaning: one who carries out a death sentence, an old sense of the word

definitions.text: who has a will to discharge
definitions.meaning: the person named in a will to carry out its terms

explanation.surface: A hangman determined to do his duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant an executioner, and now means the person appointed to carry out a dead person's will.

clue.text: What a dog may do when pleased to see a bird

definitions.text: What a dog may do when pleased
definitions.meaning: a happy dog swishes its rear appendage
a small songbird that bobs its tail

explanation.surface: A dog is pleased to spot a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy dog shakes its tail, and the same phrase names a small, slender, tail-bobbing bird.

clue.text: Hopeless outlook for an international rugger player

definitions.meaning: a prospect that is completely dark
a member of New Zealand's national rugby union team

explanation.surface: A grim outlook for a rugby international.
explanation.walkthrough: New Zealand's rugby team is named for its black kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A totally dark prospect is gloomy, and New Zealand's rugby players are named after their black kit.

clue.text: Train horse to commit burglary

definitions.meaning: to tame a young horse for riding
to force entry into a building to steal

explanation.surface: Teaching a horse to burgle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to tame a young horse and also to enter a building by force.

clue.text: He is disaffected to some degree if not to a fault

definitions.text: He is disaffected to some degree

parts.note: a defect is a fault or flaw
or, as in 'some if not all'

explanation.surface: A man is somewhat unhappy, if not excessively so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a fault' looks like the idiom for excessively, but 'a fault' gives the flaw word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons their side or country is disaffected enough to switch allegiance.

clue.text: The echoing sound of a horn

indicators.note: an echo repeats the same thing back, so the word reads identically in reverse

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A horn's blast bounces back.
explanation.definitionFit: A short blast from a car or ship horn.

clue.text: Suitable fabric for a lady of fifty one?

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Asking what material suits a woman of fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty one' reads as an age, but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate openwork fabric is traditionally associated with ladies' clothing.

clue.text: One who keeps stock to frighten a fellow

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A stockkeeper sets out to scare a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhand looks after cattle, which are livestock.

clue.text: Hitches a horse amidship

annotationWithheld.why: 'Hitches a horse amidship': the wordplay needs NAG inside SS (ship), but the single printed word 'amidship' would have to give both SS and the container indicator.

clue.text: Specious fees returned to hearten the Post Office

indicators.note: to put at the heart, so one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for fees is read backwards

parts.note: dues are fees

explanation.surface: Bogus fees sent back to cheer the Post Office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To hearten' looks like encouragement, but here it means put at the heart: the reversed fees go in the middle of the Post Office abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sham is false though it looks genuine, which is what specious means.

clue.text: Making provision for everyone beset by outstanding debts

indicators.note: everyone is followed and pressed by the debts, so that word comes first

parts.note: all means everyone
owing describes money still due

explanation.surface: Everyone is surrounded by unpaid bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitting or budgeting for something is to make room for it.

clue.text: A stupid fellow when upset becomes withdrawn

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word for a stupid fellow is written backwards

parts.note: a fool is a stupid fellow

explanation.surface: An idiot who gets upset turns sullen and distant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved and distant keeps apart from others.

clue.text: Let off-from a prosecution apparently

definitions.meaning: to fire a gun or release a defendant
read as dis- plus charge, freed from an accusation

explanation.surface: A defendant is let off from a prosecution.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire or release is one sense, and a court freeing someone of a charge is the other.
